query: Invent an orthography for a five-tone language where each word is traced as a single continuous line without detached marks and remains legible when turned upside down.
Devise a twenty-minute classroom activity that teaches eight-year-olds how price inflation works using only wooden building blocks, no spoken or written numbers, and no play money.
Develop a five-minute murder mystery play for three actors on an empty stage that uses no spoken words, props, or lighting changes, yet clearly reveals the killer's motive.
Invent a childproof kitchen cabinet latch made from at most three pieces of carved wood, using no metal, springs, magnets, or glue, that resets automatically whenever the door closes.
How would you shape a soap bar so even wear changes its outline from rabbit to fish to tortoise while preserving one connected, usable piece?
Design a coat that becomes a backpack using only fabric and thread, with no detachable parts and every pocket usable in both forms.
Invent a wedding ceremony for a couple on opposite riverbanks, where nobody speaks and no person or object crosses the water.
Propose a pharmaceutical vial anti-counterfeiting tag made entirely of edible biodegradable materials that any smartphone camera can verify with a drop of tap water yet no printer can duplicate.
Devise a way to fill a 150-seat legislature with no voting whatsoever that gives every adult citizen an identical chance of serving while guaranteeing each committee verifiable domain expertise.
Plan how a 13th-century merchant could deliver live North Sea eels to a banquet in Vienna using no ice, no salt, and a single wagon.
If all wooden objects gradually grew back into living trees, design a furniture-making tradition that balances daily comfort with the fate of cherished heirlooms.

Outline an archaeological excavation strategy for a world where artifacts answer questions about their makers but lose one physical feature with every answer, balancing testimony against preservation.
Make a postal service workable when every handwritten letter doubles in weight for each mile separating it from its writer, covering delivery, pricing, and undelivered mail.
If human conception were possible only during two weeks each spring, design a national obstetric care system adapted to the resulting seasonal birth surge.
If animal and insect pollination had never evolved and all terrestrial flora relied exclusively on wind or water for reproduction, how would human agriculture and nutrition develop?
Imagine if human skin involuntarily turned bright red in anger, blue in fear, and yellow when lying, and describe how high-stakes diplomacy and summit protocols would evolve.

If tactile knot-and-cord encoding like the Andean khipu had become humanity's sole writing medium instead of visual scripts, how would information technology evolve from archives to digital computing?
Suppose Earth never generated a magnetic field yet somehow kept its atmosphere and biosphere, and trace how fifteenth-century Portuguese ocean navigation would have developed without any compass.
Suppose horses had died out in Eurasia at the Pleistocene's end as in the Americas, and trace how steppe nomadism, land warfare, and overland trade would have unfolded before 1500.

If private property had always legally vanished at its owner's death, with no inheritance or bequest possible anywhere in history, how would family structures and long-term capital formation have evolved?
Design a grocery assortment policy using island biogeography (colonization, extinction, species-area relationships) to govern product introductions and removals across differently sized stores.
Translate the mechanics of canal locks into a neighborhood dispute-mediation process, mapping water levels, paired gates, and staged passage to concrete rules for reaching agreements.
Apply the logic of electrical circuits (switches, fuses, parallel paths) to design a babysitting network for five families that survives one caregiver's cancellation.
How could error correction (repairing damaged messages) shape a treasure hunt whose players can find the prize even when some clues are missing and others lie?
Map the compositional structure of perfumery (top notes, middle notes, base notes, evaporation) onto the guest experience of a boutique hotel from check-in to a month after checkout.
Apply the techniques of stage magic (misdirection, forced choice, sleight of hand, the reveal) to designing a parent's nightly bedtime routine for a reluctant four-year-old.
Apply the principles of optics (refraction, focal length, magnification, prism dispersion) to the process by which a courtroom jury evaluates conflicting eyewitness testimony during a trial.
Model a family bakery's handover to the next generation on honeybee swarming, where scout bees inspect sites and dance until enough agree on one new home.
Use the mechanics of a loom (fixed warp threads, a shuttle carrying the weft across, alternate threads lifted to open a path) to schedule a twelve-team soccer season on three fields.
Apply the ecology of forest fires (fuel buildup, controlled burns, pinecones that open only in heat) to managing the clutter in a family's three-bedroom house across twenty years.
Design a three-chef kitchen relay system that forces the invention of unprecedented dishes by strictly limiting which senses each chef may use to inspect the previous chef's work.
Invent a musical notation system for an acoustic quartet that specifies no notes or rhythms, only rules for how each player must transform or contradict what another just played.
Design a shelving system for a physical library that arranges books not by topic or popularity, but to trigger unexpected creative leaps whenever a reader compares two neighboring volumes.
Outline a school curriculum that trains students to invent original questions rather than answers by finding everyday situations where two standard textbooks make contradictory predictions.
Design a shop that lends unfinished household inventions for seven days, accepting a working new feature as payment instead of money.
Invent a yearly ritual for an imaginary religion that trains worshippers to create new sacred symbols while keeping the same three teachings recognizable.
Design a card deck that helps photographers invent new pictures of one kitchen chair by pairing instructions about what to reveal and what to hide.
Build a choreographic-originality score computed solely from motion-capture data that separates genuine invention from randomness and from the choreographer's own habitual movement signature.
Design a children's building set whose physical pieces themselves make repeating a previously built structure harder than inventing a new one, with the difficulty growing over months of play.
Design a hiking club's challenge in which members repeatedly redraw the same two-mile trail and earn rank only for features that another member can locate yet every earlier map missed.
Invent a new spectator sport whose outcome is decided by a quantity that no existing sport has ever scored, grounded in a real measurable human capacity.
How might a small town respond to a serious assault so that, a year later, both the attacker and the victim are measurably safer and more trusted than before?
Invent a skilled manual trade, complete with its own tools and apprenticeship, that no society has ever practiced yet a town of five thousand would employ year-round.
Design a multi-generational selective-breeding blueprint that would turn a specific real wild organism, never before domesticated, into a novel agricultural or industrial staple.
Invent an entirely new kind of holiday that passes from household to household like a borrowed book, without marking births, anniversaries, or religious events.
What could a public drinking fountain become if every drink helped build a lasting, useful object, and how would this unprecedented fountain work?
Invent a new form of ownership for a village orchard that is neither private, shared, nor public, yet still settles who may pick its apples.
Propose an entirely new category of forensic evidence based on a verifiable physical, chemical, or biological trace of human activity that standard investigative protocols completely overlook.
Develop a household object made from clay, timber, and natural fibers that improves its primary domestic function each time it is accidentally dropped or broken.
Invent a category of domestic furniture built around a common human posture that chairs, beds, and tables ignore, specifying its mechanics and how it reshapes a room's social life.
